text: The sandbox remains one rwb_sandbox database with schema public for the ACE-shaped test double, schema recovery for the 30 v_ace_* views and the three helper functions, and 19 rwb_* schemas; the 19 baselines are applied in the wave order of Architecture v5 slide 41 and each schema is seeded after its own baseline; seed 20261128 and the 2,812-case volume stay the total and are split by the owning service named in the Ownership Map; a table owned by the platform is seeded in the schema of the service that writes it. A login that is not yet created fails the preflight by name rather than producing a partial sandbox.
why: No source states the per-schema seed volumes, the build order across 19 baselines or whether the sandbox keeps one database; the legacy story fixes one database, one recovery schema, one seed and one volume, and the split estate still has to be seeded from tables that now live in 19 schemas.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4, 11 and 13; Arch v5 slides 8, 9, 20 and 41; Ownership Map v1 tables.
confirm: Solution architect and ACE DBA at the wave-1 sandbox review
impact: No business value changes: seed 20261128, the 2,812 cases, the 10 percent inventory split and the 30 views stay as the legacy story fixes them; only the schema each row lands in is decided here.

text: The ledger append is a one-hop REST command on rwb-source-data. P1 writes the entry, the local decision record and the outbox row in one transaction in rwb_source_data and answers 201 with the entry ID and case_seq; a repeated Idempotency-Key returns the first entry; a write failure answers 503 with MSG-P1-022 and leaves no entry and no action; the caller treats a non-2xx as a failed action and retries or compensates through its own saga, so no action is kept without its entry.
why: The legacy append is in-process and in-transaction; the target moves it to another service, and no source defines the remote contract or the failure semantics that replace Propagation.MANDATORY.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-066 sections 3, 4, 12 and 13; Ownership Map v1 api and table interaction; Arch v5 slides 11, 15 and 41; Template and Rules section R3 default ruling and section R5.5 DP-18.
confirm: Solution architect, rwb-source-data owner and rwb-case owner at the interaction contract review
impact: The ledger stays append-only and one per case; the 503 with MSG-P1-022, the 201 with the entry and the one-entry-on-retry rule are unchanged; only the transport from the caller to P1 is new.

text: The P3 case action and the P1 ledger entry are one business transaction without a distributed transaction: the caller writes the P1 entry first through the one-hop contract and commits its own case action only after a 201, and on a P1 failure it leaves the action uncommitted or compensates it and records the compensated state; the case then shows its previous state and no ledger entry.
why: The legacy append shares the caller's transaction; after the split the P1 write and the P3 change are two local transactions, and no source names the mechanism that keeps them one business outcome.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-066 sections 3, 4 and 12; Arch v5 slide 11 (Idempotency-Key, one hop, 2 s); Ownership Map v1 table interaction and api POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions owner P1.
confirm: Solution architect, rwb-source-data owner and rwb-case owner at the interaction contract review
impact: No business value changes: the action and the entry still succeed or fail together; only the mechanism moves from one transaction to an ordered call with compensation.

text: P1 rwb-source-data runs one consumer group across rwb.case.events.v1, rwb.document.events.v1 and rwb.decision-record.v1, accepts the current and the previous schema version of each event, dedupes on the CloudEvents id in rwb_source_data.processed_event and keeps the event idempotency key as the business key, and assigns case_seq under the case lock at append; entries are read in occurredAt order and a cross-topic inversion that occurredAt cannot resolve is reported by the run, not reordered silently.
why: The legacy listener sees one ordered outbox; the target sees three topics with independent partitions, and no source defines the map, the versions, the group or the cross-topic order.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-067 sections 3, 4, 8 and 12; Arch v5 slides 11, 14, 16, 42 and 43; Ownership Map v1 events EV-01, EV-02, EV-04, EV-08, EV-16 and EV-19.
confirm: Solution architect, rwb-source-data owner and the three producer owners at the wave-1 event review
impact: The six event codes, the append-only ledger, the one-entry rule and the retry/DLT behaviour are unchanged; only the topics, the group and the cross-topic order rule are decided here.

text: The ledger listener of rwb-source-data is an additional consumer group on rwb.case.events.v1 and rwb.document.events.v1, in addition to the consumers listed on Architecture v5 slide 42, and on the shared rwb.decision-record.v1; no existing consumer group or event type changes.
why: The event catalogue names rwb-agent, rwb-deviation, rwb-reporting, rwb-case and rwb-comms as consumers of the case and document topics and does not name the ledger listener, while the target ledger needs the six events.
read: Arch v5 slides 42 and 43 (consumer lists); legacy RWB-E1-067 section 3 and BR1; Template and Rules DP-09 and DP-18.
confirm: Solution architect and rwb-source-data owner at the wave-1 event review
impact: The catalogue's existing consumers and event types are unchanged; the ledger listener is an additive consumer group, so no producer changes.

text: A ledger event that exhausts the retry topics is dead-lettered on the .dlt topic of its own topic, raises LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED for its case and carries MSG-P1-022 in the incident detail; it is replayed only after the contract version it names is registered, and a replay adds one entry and leaves the earlier entries intact.
why: The legacy exception queue is a single queue with an owner; the target has one .dlt per topic and no source fixes the incident code, the message detail or the replay gate for the ledger listener.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-067 sections 4, 5 and 8 (BR5); Arch v5 slides 11 and 22 (retry then .dlt and alert); Template and Rules DP-09 and DP-18.
confirm: Solution architect and platform event owner at the wave-1 event review
impact: No event type or business value changes; a poison event is not written and never blocks the entries before it.

text: The 30 v_ace_* views stay in schema recovery owned by ace_view_owner; the rwb_source_data login holds SELECT on the views and no privilege in public; each of the other 18 service logins holds no privilege on public or on the views and reads only its own schema; PUBLIC holds nothing; BND-6 becomes two build rules, no class names public and no class outside rwb-source-data names a v_ace_* view or another service's schema, with the allowed list read from the module map and the 19 login names taken from Environment and Deployment Design when issued.
why: The legacy story has one recovery login and one recovery schema; the target has 19 logins and a view schema that is separate from every service schema, and no source fixes the login names or the full grant matrix.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-069 sections 3, 4, 12 and 13; Arch v5 slides 8, 9, 11 and 41; Ownership Map v1 extension tables; Template and Rules DP-02 and DP-05.
confirm: ACE DBA, solution architect and rwb-source-data owner at the wave-1 boundary review
impact: No view definition, field ID or business rule changes; only the login list and the split of the grant matrix are decided here, and a missing login fails the preflight by name.

text: Each service registers exactly one worker on queue rwb-<short> in namespace rwb-recovery, with its own workload identity and a client certificate naming the service; the queues are created at platform install from the service catalogue and a worker that polls another service's queue fails the run; each service has its own codec key under the namespace key; the durability probe starts the smoke workflow on one service queue named in configuration, while the 06:00 JOB-22 platform run stays with RWB-PLT-E1070-APP.
why: The legacy story builds the cluster and one namespace; the target adds 19 workers and 19 queues, and no source fixes the identity, certificate, registration, queue creation or codec-key contract per service.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-070 sections 3, 4, 12 and 13; Arch v5 slides 8, 9, 11, 23, 24 and 41; Temporal and Drools design slides 7 and 8; Ownership Map v1 PlatformSmokeWorkflow and JOB-22.
confirm: Platform team, solution architect and the service owners at the wave-1 platform review
impact: No retention, namespace, certificate authority or role mapping changes; the 19 queues and worker identities are new, and a worker on the wrong queue fails the run by name.

text: A cross-service step in this proof is one activity call on the owner's task queue under the workflow ID of the run: the smoke run calls EvaluateRules on rwb-decision and RecordAndApply on rwb-case, and the chain makes no REST call; a repeated start with the same workflow ID returns the running execution.
why: The legacy story starts a smoke workflow from a platform endpoint; the target calls another service through its activity contract, and no source fixes the call shape, the workflow ID or the repeated-start rule for this proof.
read: Arch v5 slides 11, 23, 24 and 25; Temporal and Drools design slides 7 and 8; legacy RWB-E1-070 section 12.
confirm: Platform team and solution architect at the wave-1 platform review
impact: The workflow ID remains the idempotency key and the queues stay one per service; only the probe's call path is fixed here.

text: The access review report of rwb-access is the evidence of the grant checks, and the integration suite writes its evidence beside the SIT run report in the integration evidence store; no source names that store, so the run report path is configuration.
why: The legacy story records its checks in the release evidence; the target has an access review and an integration report, and no source names where the SIT suite stores its evidence.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-070 sections 13 and 16; Arch v5 slide 14 (access review); RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG (harness).
confirm: Platform team, rwb-access owner and QA lead at the wave-1 exit review
impact: No business value changes; the report location is configuration and the grant evidence stays the access review.
